questions.q: What is the remainder when 2026 is divided by 9?
questions.x: A number leaves the same remainder mod 9 as its digit sum: 2 + 0 + 2 + 6 = 10, and 10 leaves remainder 1.

questions.q: What is the smallest positive integer divisible by every integer from 1 to 10?
questions.x: Take the highest power of each prime up to 10: 2³ × 3² × 5 × 7 = 8 × 9 × 5 × 7 = 2520.

questions.q: How many positive divisors does 360 have?
questions.x: 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5. A divisor picks each exponent independently, so there are (3 + 1)(2 + 1)(1 + 1) = 24 divisors.

questions.q: How many zeros are at the end of 100! (100 factorial)?
questions.x: Each trailing zero needs a factor 10 = 2 × 5, and 5s are scarcer. Count them: ⌊100/5⌋ + ⌊100/25⌋ = 20 + 4 = 24.

questions.q: What is the largest integer n such that 2ⁿ divides 50!?
What is the smallest positive integer that has exactly 12 positive divisors?
questions.x: 12 = 3 × 2 × 2 = 4 × 3 = 6 × 2 = 12, giving forms p²qr, p³q², p⁵q or p¹¹. Using the smallest primes, with larger exponents on smaller primes: 2² × 3 × 5 = 60, 2³ × 3² = 72, 2⁵ × 3 = 96. The smallest is 60.

questions.q: What is the last digit of 7²⁰²⁶?
questions.x: Last digits of powers of 7 cycle 7, 9, 3, 1 with period 4. 2026 = 4 × 506 + 2, so the last digit matches 7², which is 9.

questions.q: What is the remainder when 2¹⁰⁰ is divided by 7?
What are the last two digits of 3²⁰?
What is the remainder when 10¹⁰⁰ is divided by 7?
questions.x: 10 ≡ 3 (mod 7), and the powers of 3 mod 7 are 3, 2, 6, 4, 5, 1, repeating every 6. 100 = 6 × 16 + 4, so 10¹⁰⁰ ≡ 3⁴ ≡ 4.

questions.q: What is the smallest positive integer that leaves remainder 1 when divided by each of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6, and is divisible by 7?
questions.x: n − 1 is a multiple of lcm(2, 3, 4, 5, 6) = 60, so n = 61, 121, 181, 241, 301, … Checking each for divisibility by 7, the first that works is 301 = 7 × 43.

questions.q: What is the remainder when the square of any prime greater than 3 is divided by 24?
questions.x: p² − 1 = (p − 1)(p + 1). These are consecutive even numbers, so one is a multiple of 4: the product is divisible by 8. One of p − 1, p, p + 1 is a multiple of 3, and it isn't p. So 24 divides p² − 1.

questions.q: How many prime numbers are less than 50?
2026 is the product of two primes. What is the larger prime?
questions.x: 2026 = 2 × 1013. 1013 has no prime factor up to √1013 ≈ 31.8 (check 3, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 29, 31), so it is prime.

questions.q: For how many primes p are p, p + 2 and p + 4 all prime?
questions.x: p, p + 2 and p + 4 leave three different remainders mod 3, so one of them is a multiple of 3. It must equal 3 itself, which forces p = 3: giving 3, 5, 7.

questions.q: p and q are primes with p + q = 99. What is pq?
questions.x: An odd sum needs one even prime, so one of them is 2 and the other is 97. pq = 2 × 97 = 194.

questions.q: Write the binary number 1011₂ in base 10.
How many digits does 2¹⁰⁰ have? (log₁₀ 2 ≈ 0.30103)
questions.x: log₁₀(2¹⁰⁰) = 100 × 0.30103 = 30.103, so 10³⁰ ≤ 2¹⁰⁰ < 10³¹. A number between 10³⁰ and 10³¹ has 31 digits.

questions.q: How many three-digit positive integers have digits that add up to 9?
questions.x: Find a + b + c = 9 with a ≥ 1. Let a′ = a − 1: a′ + b + c = 8 with all ≥ 0. Stars and bars gives C(10, 2) = 45. No digit can exceed 9, so none need removing.

questions.q: How many integers from 1 to 1000 contain at least one digit 7?
questions.x: Count the complement. Writing 0 to 999 as three digits, 9³ = 729 have no 7. Swapping 0 for 1000 (also no 7) keeps that count for 1 to 1000. So 1000 − 729 = 271 contain a 7.

questions.q: What is the sum of the digits of 10²⁰²⁶ − 2026?
questions.x: Try a small case: 10⁶ − 2026 = 997974. In general you get (2026 − 4) = 2022 nines followed by 7974. Digit sum = 2022 × 9 + 7 + 9 + 7 + 4 = 18198 + 27 = 18225.

questions.q: If x + 1/x = 3, what is x² + 1/x²?
questions.x: Square both sides: x² + 2 + 1/x² = 9, so x² + 1/x² = 7.

questions.q: If x + 1/x = 3, what is x³ + 1/x³?
questions.x: (x + 1/x)³ = x³ + 1/x³ + 3(x + 1/x). So 27 = x³ + 1/x³ + 9, giving 18.

questions.q: a + b = 10 and ab = 21. What is a² + b²?
questions.x: a² + b² = (a + b)² − 2ab = 100 − 42 = 58. You don't need to find a and b (they are 3 and 7).

questions.q: How many pairs of positive integers (x, y) satisfy 3x + 5y = 100?
questions.x: 100 − 5y must be a positive multiple of 3, so y ≡ 2 (mod 3): y = 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17 (y = 20 would make x = 0). That is 6 pairs.

questions.q: Find the value of √(6 + √(6 + √(6 + …))), where the pattern continues forever.
questions.x: Call it x. Then x = √(6 + x), so x² − x − 6 = 0, giving (x − 3)(x + 2) = 0. x is positive, so x = 3.

questions.q: a and b are the roots of x² − 5x + 3 = 0. What is a³ + b³?
questions.x: a + b = 5 and ab = 3. a³ + b³ = (a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b) = 125 − 45 = 80.

questions.q: a and b are the roots of x² − 5x + 3 = 0. What is 1/a² + 1/b²?
questions.x: 1/a² + 1/b² = (a² + b²)/(ab)². a² + b² = (a + b)² − 2ab = 25 − 6 = 19, and (ab)² = 9, giving 19/9. Forgetting the −2ab gives 25/9.

questions.q: What is the minimum value of x² − 6x + 13 for real x?
questions.x: Complete the square: x² − 6x + 13 = (x − 3)² + 4. The square is at least 0, so the minimum is 4, at x = 3.

questions.q: x and y are real numbers with x + y = 10. What is the largest possible value of xy?
questions.x: xy = x(10 − x) = 25 − (x − 5)², which is largest when x = y = 5, giving 25.

questions.q: What is the minimum value of x + 4/x for x > 0?
questions.x: By AM–GM, x + 4/x ≥ 2√(x × 4/x) = 2 × 2 = 4, with equality when x = 4/x, i.e. x = 2.

questions.q: a and b are positive real numbers with a + b = 1. What is the minimum value of (1 + 1/a)(1 + 1/b)?
questions.x: Expanding, the product is 1 + 1/a + 1/b + 1/(ab) = 1 + (a + b)/(ab) + 1/(ab) = 1 + 2/(ab). AM–GM gives ab ≤ 1/4, so the product is at least 1 + 8 = 9, when a = b = ½.
Pair the first and last terms: 1 + 100 = 2 + 99 = … = 101, with 50 pairs. 50 × 101 = 5050.
The sum of the first n odd numbers is n². There are 50 odd numbers from 1 to 99, so the sum is 50² = 2500.

questions.q: The 5th term of an arithmetic sequence is 17 and the 12th term is 38. What is the 20th term?
questions.x: 7 steps take the sequence from 17 to 38, so the common difference is 21/7 = 3. The 20th term is 8 steps after the 12th: 38 + 24 = 62.
Each term splits: 1/(n(n + 1)) = 1/n − 1/(n + 1). The sum telescopes to 1 − 1/100 = 99/100.

questions.q: Find the sum of 1/(√n + √(n + 1)) for n = 1, 2, 3, …, 99.
questions.x: Rationalise: 1/(√n + √(n + 1)) = √(n + 1) − √n. The sum telescopes to √100 − √1 = 10 − 1 = 9.

questions.q: A sequence has a₁ = 1, a₂ = 3 and aₙ₊₂ = aₙ₊₁ − aₙ for n ≥ 1. What is a₂₀₂₆?
questions.x: Writing out the terms gives 1, 3, 2, −1, −3, −2, 1, 3, … so the sequence repeats every 6. 2026 = 6 × 337 + 4, so a₂₀₂₆ = a₄ = −1.

questions.q: f(x) = 2x + 3. What is f(f(1))?
What is the remainder when x³ − 2x + 5 is divided by x − 2?
questions.x: By the remainder theorem, the remainder is the value at x = 2: 8 − 4 + 5 = 9.

questions.q: For all x ≠ 0, f(x) + 2f(1/x) = 3x. What is f(2)?
questions.x: Put x = 2: f(2) + 2f(½) = 6. Put x = ½: f(½) + 2f(2) = 3/2. Solving these two equations together gives f(2) = −1 and f(½) = 7/2.

questions.q: A polynomial p(x) has p(1) = 3 and p(2) = 5. What is the remainder when p(x) is divided by (x − 1)(x − 2)?
questions.x: The remainder has degree below 2, so write it as ax + b. Then a + b = 3 and 2a + b = 5, giving a = 2, b = 1: 2x + 1.

questions.q: f is a function from real numbers to real numbers with f(x)f(y) − f(xy) = x + y for all real x, y. What is f(2)?
questions.x: x = y = 0 gives f(0)² = f(0), so f(0) is 0 or 1. Then y = 0 gives f(0)(f(x) − 1) = x. f(0) = 0 would force x = 0 for every x, so f(0) = 1 and f(x) = x + 1. This works, and f(2) = 3.

questions.q: How many different arrangements of the letters of MATH are there?
questions.x: Four different letters: 4! = 24.

questions.q: How many different arrangements of the letters of LEVEL are there?
questions.x: 5 letters with L and E each repeated twice: 5!/(2! × 2!) = 120/4 = 30.

questions.q: How many diagonals does a convex decagon (10 sides) have?
questions.x: Each vertex joins to 7 others by a diagonal (not itself or its 2 neighbours). 10 × 7 counts each diagonal twice, so there are 70/2 = 35.

questions.q: On a grid, you walk from (0, 0) to (4, 4), moving only one unit right or one unit up at each step. How many different paths are there?
questions.x: Every path is 8 steps, 4 of them right. Choose which 4: C(8, 4) = 70.

questions.q: In how many ways can 5 people sit around a round table, if rotations of the same seating count as the same?
questions.x: Fix one person's seat to remove rotations, then arrange the other 4: 4! = 24.

questions.q: How many solutions in non-negative integers does x + y + z = 10 have?
questions.x: Stars and bars: arrange 10 stars and 2 bars in a row, giving C(12, 2) = 66.

questions.q: How many integers from 1 to 100 are divisible by 2, 3 or 5?
questions.x: Inclusion–exclusion: 50 + 33 + 20 − 16 − 10 − 6 + 3 = 74. (16 multiples of 6, 10 of 10, 6 of 15, 3 of 30.)

questions.q: Four letters are put into four addressed envelopes at random, one per envelope. In how many ways can every letter end up in the wrong envelope?
Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the total is 7?
questions.x: 6 of the 36 equally likely outcomes give 7: (1, 6), (2, 5), (3, 4), (4, 3), (5, 2), (6, 1). 6/36 = 1/6. 1/11 wrongly treats the 11 totals as equally likely.

questions.q: Three fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
questions.x: P(no heads) = (½)³ = 1/8, so P(at least one head) = 1 − 1/8 = 7/8.

questions.q: A bag has 3 red and 5 blue balls. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability both are red?
questions.x: P = 3/8 × 2/7 = 6/56 = 3/28. With replacement it would be 9/64.

questions.q: A two-digit number is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is a perfect square?
questions.x: The two-digit squares are 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81: 6 out of 90 numbers (10 to 99). 6/90 = 1/15.

questions.q: Three fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the total is 10?
questions.x: Count ordered triples from 1 to 6 summing to 10. The sets {1,3,6}, {1,4,5}, {2,3,5} give 6 orders each (18); {2,2,6}, {2,4,4}, {3,3,4} give 3 each (9). 27/216 = 1/8.

questions.q: At a party, 10 people each shake hands once with every other person. How many handshakes are there?
questions.x: Each handshake is a pair of people: C(10, 2) = 10 × 9 / 2 = 45.

questions.q: A drawer has socks in 4 colours. In the dark, what is the smallest number of socks you must take to be sure of a matching pair?
questions.x: With 4 socks you might get one of each colour. A 5th must repeat a colour (pigeonhole principle).

questions.q: What is the smallest number of people needed to be sure that at least 3 of them were born in the same month?
questions.x: 24 people could be split 2 per month across 12 months. One more forces some month to have 3: 2 × 12 + 1 = 25.

questions.q: What is the smallest number of integers you must choose from 1, 2, …, 20 to be sure that two of them add up to 21?
questions.x: Split the numbers into 10 pairs that add to 21: (1, 20), (2, 19), …, (10, 11). You can choose 10 numbers, one from each pair, without success; the 11th completes a pair.

questions.q: On an island, knights always tell the truth and knaves always lie. A says, 'B is a knave.' B says, 'A and I are the same type.' What are A and B?
o: A is a knight and B is a knave.
A is a knave and B is a knight.
questions.x: If A were a knave, B would be a knight; but then B's claim that they're the same type would be false, which a knight can't say. So A is a knight and B is a knave. B's claim is then false, which fits.

questions.q: What is the smaller angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 3:40? Give your answer in degrees.
questions.x: The minute hand is at 40 × 6° = 240°. The hour hand moves 0.5° per minute: 3 × 30° + 40 × 0.5° = 110°. The difference is 130°.

questions.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon, in degrees?
questions.x: An n-gon splits into n − 2 triangles from one vertex: (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°.

questions.q: What is the size of each interior angle of a regular octagon, in degrees?
questions.x: Each exterior angle is 360°/8 = 45°, so each interior angle is 180° − 45° = 135°.

questions.q: What is the area of a triangle with sides 13, 14 and 15?
questions.x: Heron's formula: s = 21, area = √(21 × 8 × 7 × 6) = √7056 = 84. Or split it with the altitude of 12 to the side 14: pieces 5 and 9 (5-12-13 and 9-12-15 triangles), area ½ × 14 × 12 = 84.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has legs 5 and 12. What is the length of the altitude to the hypotenuse?
questions.x: The hypotenuse is 13. Area = ½ × 5 × 12 = 30 = ½ × 13 × h, so h = 60/13.

questions.q: What is the radius of the inscribed circle of a triangle with sides 6, 8 and 10?
questions.x: Area = ½ × 6 × 8 = 24 and the semi-perimeter s = 12. Inradius = area / s = 2. For a right triangle, r = (a + b − c)/2 = (6 + 8 − 10)/2 = 2 as well.

questions.q: In triangle ABC, AB = 6, AC = 9 and BC = 10. The bisector of angle A meets BC at D. What is BD?
questions.x: Angle bisector theorem: BD : DC = AB : AC = 6 : 9 = 2 : 3. So BD = 2/5 × 10 = 4.

questions.q: Triangle ABC has area 36 and centroid G. What is the area of triangle GBC?
questions.x: G lies a third of the way up the median from BC, so its height above BC is a third of A's. Area GBC = 36/3 = 12.

questions.q: In triangle ABC, D is on AB and E is on AC with DE parallel to BC and AD : DB = 2 : 3. What is the ratio of the area of triangle ADE to the area of quadrilateral DBCE?
questions.x: ADE is similar to ABC with scale factor AD/AB = 2/5, so its area is 4/25 of ABC. The quadrilateral is the remaining 21/25, giving 4 : 21. 4 : 25 compares ADE with the whole triangle.

questions.q: AB is a diameter of a circle and C is another point on the circle. What is angle ACB, in degrees?
questions.x: The angle in a semicircle is a right angle (it is half the 180° angle at the centre).

questions.q: An arc subtends 140° at the centre of a circle. What angle does it subtend at a point on the rest of the circumference, in degrees?
questions.x: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference, so the answer is 140°/2 = 70°.

questions.q: A chord of length 16 is in a circle of radius 10. How far is the chord from the centre?
questions.x: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, forming a right triangle with hypotenuse 10 and leg 8. The distance is √(100 − 64) = 6.

questions.q: A point P is 13 units from the centre of a circle of radius 5. What is the length of a tangent from P to the circle?
questions.x: The radius meets the tangent at a right angle, so the tangent length is √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12.

questions.q: From an external point P, a tangent PT has length 6. A line through P cuts the circle at A and B, with PA = 4 and B further from P. What is AB?
questions.x: Tangent–secant theorem: PA × PB = PT², so 4 × PB = 36 and PB = 9. AB = PB − PA = 5.

questions.q: A circle is inscribed in a square of side 10, and a smaller square is inscribed in that circle. What is the area of the smaller square?
questions.x: The circle has diameter 10, which is the diagonal of the small square. A square with diagonal d has area d²/2 = 100/2 = 50.

questions.q: Two circles of radii 9 and 4 touch externally. What is the length of their common external tangent, between the two points of contact?
questions.x: The centres are 9 + 4 = 13 apart. Sliding the tangent segment to the centre line makes a right triangle with hypotenuse 13 and one leg 9 − 4 = 5, so the tangent is √(169 − 25) = 12.

questions.q: What is the distance between the points (1, 2) and (7, 10)?
What is the area of the triangle with vertices (1, 2), (4, 6) and (7, 2)?
questions.x: The base from (1, 2) to (7, 2) is horizontal, with length 6. The height is 6 − 2 = 4, so the area is ½ × 6 × 4 = 12.

questions.q: How many points with integer coordinates lie on the line segment from (0, 0) to (12, 18), including the endpoints?
questions.x: gcd(12, 18) = 6, so the segment splits into 6 equal steps of (2, 3). That gives 6 + 1 = 7 lattice points.

questions.q: How many points with integer coordinates lie strictly inside the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (10, 0) and (0, 10)?
questions.x: Interior points have x, y ≥ 1 and x + y ≤ 9. For x = 1 to 8 there are 9 − x choices of y: 8 + 7 + … + 1 = 36. Pick's theorem agrees: 50 = I + 30/2 − 1, so I = 36.
